source.subject: Biology
source.unit: Unit 1 — Diversity in the Living World
source.source_scope: Only the content printed on PDF page 9 (printed page 18): the rest of Section 2.3.2 Ascomycetes, Section 2.3.3 Basidiomycetes and Section 2.3.4 Deuteromycetes.

questions.question: In ascomycetes the mycelium is:
questions.explanation: The page says the mycelium of ascomycetes is branched and septate.
questions.source_text: is branched and septate. The asexual spores are conidia

questions.question: In ascomycetes, conidia are produced exogenously on special mycelium called:
questions.explanation: The page says the asexual spores, conidia, are produced exogenously on special mycelium called conidiophores.
questions.source_text: The asexual spores are conidia produced exogenously on the special mycelium called conidiophores.

questions.question: Ascospores of ascomycetes are produced endogenously in sac-like structures called:
questions.explanation: The page says ascospores are produced endogenously in sac like asci (singular ascus).
questions.source_text: Sexual spores are called ascospores which are produced endogenously in sac like asci (singular ascus).

questions.question: Asci are arranged in different types of fruiting bodies called:
questions.explanation: The page says the asci are arranged in fruiting bodies called ascocarps.
questions.source_text: These asci are arranged in different types of fruiting bodies called ascocarps.

questions.question: Which of the following are examples of ascomycetes given on this page?
questions.explanation: The page gives Aspergillus, Claviceps and Neurospora. Agaricus and Ustilago are basidiomycetes.
questions.source_text: Some examples are Aspergillus (Figure 2.5b), Claviceps and Neurospora.

questions.question: Which ascomycete is used extensively in biochemical and genetic work?
questions.explanation: The page says Neurospora is used extensively in biochemical and genetic work.
questions.source_text: Neurospora is used extensively in biochemical and genetic work.

questions.question: Morels and truffles are:
questions.explanation: The page says many members like morels and truffles are edible and are considered delicacies, in the discussion of ascomycetes.
questions.source_text: Many members like morels and truffles are edible and are considered delicacies.

questions.question: Commonly known forms of basidiomycetes are:
questions.explanation: The page lists mushrooms, bracket fungi and puffballs.
questions.source_text: Commonly known forms of basidiomycetes are mushrooms, bracket fungi or puffballs.

questions.question: Rusts and smuts, which grow in living plant bodies as parasites, belong to:
questions.explanation: The page cites rusts and smuts as parasitic basidiomycetes.
questions.source_text: in living plant bodies as parasites, e.g., rusts and smuts.

questions.question: In basidiomycetes, asexual spores are generally not found, but vegetative reproduction occurs commonly by:
questions.explanation: The page says asexual spores are generally not found, but vegetative reproduction by fragmentation is common.
questions.source_text: The asexual spores are generally not found, but vegetative reproduction by fragmentation is common.

questions.question: In basidiomycetes, plasmogamy is brought about by:
options: Fusion of two nuclei in the basidium
Fusion of two vegetative or somatic cells of different strains or genotypes
questions.explanation: The page says sex organs are absent, and plasmogamy happens by fusion of two vegetative or somatic cells of different strains or genotypes.
questions.source_text: The sex organs are absent, but plasmogamy is brought about by fusion of two vegetative or somatic cells of different strains or genotypes.

questions.question: In basidiomycetes, karyogamy and meiosis take place in the basidium, producing:
questions.explanation: The page says they produce four basidiospores.
questions.source_text: Karyogamy and meiosis take place in the basidium producing four basidiospores.

questions.question: Basidiospores are produced on the basidium in which way, and where are basidia arranged?
options: Exogenously; in fruiting bodies called basidiocarps
questions.explanation: The page says basidiospores are exogenously produced on the basidium and basidia are arranged in basidiocarps.
questions.source_text: The basidiospores are exogenously produced on the basidium (pl.: basidia). The basidia are arranged in fruiting bodies called basidiocarps.

questions.question: Which of the following are common basidiomycetes named on the page?
questions.explanation: The page names Agaricus, Ustilago and Puccinia. Neurospora is an ascomycete and Trichoderma a deuteromycete.
questions.source_text: Some common members are Agaricus (mushroom) (Figure 2.5c), Ustilago (smut) and Puccinia (rust fungus).

questions.question: Deuteromycetes are commonly known as imperfect fungi because:
options: Only their asexual or vegetative phases are known
questions.explanation: The page gives this as the reason for the name imperfect fungi.
questions.source_text: Commonly known as imperfect fungi because only the asexual or vegetative phases of these fungi are known.

questions.question: When the sexual forms of imperfect fungi were discovered, the fungi were:
options: Moved into the classes they rightly belong to
questions.explanation: The page says that when the sexual forms were discovered they were moved into the classes they rightly belong to, often ascomycetes and basidiomycetes.
questions.source_text: When the sexual forms of these fungi were discovered they were moved into classes they rightly belong to.

questions.question: Deuteromycetes reproduce only by:
questions.explanation: The page says deuteromycetes reproduce only by asexual spores known as conidia, and their mycelium is septate and branched.
questions.source_text: The deuteromycetes reproduce only by asexual spores known as conidia.

questions.question: A large number of deuteromycetes are:
options: Decomposers of litter that help in mineral cycling
questions.explanation: The page says a large number of them are decomposers of litter and help in mineral cycling.
questions.source_text: a large number of them are decomposers of litter and help in mineral cycling.

questions.question: Which of these are examples of deuteromycetes?
questions.explanation: The page gives Alternaria, Colletotrichum and Trichoderma. Claviceps is an ascomycete and Puccinia a basidiomycete.
questions.source_text: Some examples are Alternaria, Colletotrichum and Trichoderma.

questions.question: Match each class of fungi with its spore-bearing structure or feature from this page.
questions.explanation: Ascomycetes bear spores in asci, basidiomycetes on basidia, and deuteromycetes reproduce only by conidia.
questions.source_text: sac like asci (singular ascus) ... Karyogamy and meiosis take place in the basidium ... reproduce only by asexual spores known as conidia.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. Ascospores are produced endogenously in asci.
2. Basidiospores are produced endogenously inside the basidium.
3. Basidiospores are produced exogenously on the basidium.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 match the page. Statement 2 is false because basidiospores are produced exogenously on the basidium.
questions.source_text: which are produced endogenously in sac like asci ... The basidiospores are exogenously produced on the basidium

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Deuteromycetes are called imperfect fungi.
Reason (R): Only the asexual or vegetative phases of these fungi are known.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation: The page gives the lack of a known sexual phase as the reason for the name.
questions.source_text: Commonly known as imperfect fungi because only the asexual or vegetative phases of these fungi are known.
